question: arXiv:1410.3696v1 derives the isotropic diffuse gamma-ray background with three reference foreground models, A, B and C. Why do the authors go beyond the class of Galactic diffuse emission models studied before, to which model A belongs, and in what do models B and C differ from model A?

arguments.answer: Why go beyond model A: Model A comes from the GALPROP-based DGE class of Ackermann et al. 2012. That class covers only a limited set of propagation and injection scenarios, with a constant diffusion coefficient throughout the Galaxy and the same source population injecting electrons and nuclei. The authors show (Appendix A) that IC templates from such models are inconsistent in the multi-component likelihood fit; for example, the predicted IC spectrum does not match the one fitted to the LAT data. An inaccurate IC intensity distribution could be partly compensated by the isotropic template and so bias the IGRB. They therefore add two models with more degrees of freedom. Differences: Model A has CR nuclei and electron sources tracing the pulsar distribution, with constant diffusion coefficient and re-acceleration strength. Model B allows distinct electron and nuclei source populations. It adds an electron-only source population near the Galactic centre that produces most of the IC emission, plus a local source of soft electrons needed to explain the electron spectrum below 20 GV. Its electron spectrum is tuned to the observed IC emission rather than the measured CR electron spectrum. Model C lets the diffusion coefficient and re-acceleration strength vary with Galactocentric radius and height above the plane. Its CR sources are more centrally peaked than the pulsar distribution.
